newsitem.title: USA: Newmont says low production costs favor its bid.
newsitem.headline: Newmont says low production costs favor its bid.

text.p: Newmont Mining Corp Chairman Ronald Cambre on Tuesday said one reason that Santa Fe Pacific Gold Corp shareholders should support his company's hostile bid for Santa Fe is Newmont's low gold-production costs.
Low production costs are especially important given the recent fall in bullion prices, he said.

Earlier Tuesday, Newmont sweetened its unwelcome proposal to acquire Santa Fe, offering to 0.4 Newmont shares for each Santa Fe share. The move is designed to thwart Santa Fe's friendly merger deal with Homestake Mining Co.
Early last month, Santa Fe rebuffed Newmont's offer of 0.33 share for each Santa Fe share, or about $2.0 billion.

When the Newmont offer was announced on December 5, Newmont shares finished with a 3/8 gain at 47-1/8, a level that valued Santa Fe at $15.55 per share. Santa Fe Pacific finished the day at 14-7/8, up three.
Four days later on December 9, it announced a merger pact with Homestake Mining, which offered 1.115 Homestake share for each Santa Fe share.
Terms of the rival deal then valued Santa Fe at $17.42 per share, or $2.3 billion in stock.
But over the last month, gold stocks have continued to fall as the price of gold declined almost $9 per ounce since early last month to about $360.
Cambre said Newmont's $202-per-ounce cash cost of gold production would rise to only $215 if it merged with Santa Fe. That is about equal to Santa Fe's current cost of production.
If the Homestake merger goes through, he said, shareholders would face higher production costs because Homestake's cash cost per ounce is $248 per ounce, he added.
